newsitem.title: USA: Polaroid plan on track for coming quarters.
newsitem.headline: Polaroid plan on track for coming quarters.

text.p: Polaroid Corp said Wednesday its operating plan was on track for coming quarters and it will continue to monitor the impact of the strong dollar on its business.

For the first quarter, the company reported earnings of $0.13 per share, excluding net after-tax exchange gains, compared to a year-earlier loss of $0.07 before charges for restructuring and other expenses and a gain on the sale of real estate.

Operating profit in the first quarter of 1997 was $19.2 million compared to $4.5 million, excluding pre-tax special charges for restructuring and other expenses of $110.0 million, in the same period last year.
Polaroid said its 1997 increase is primarily due to increased U.S. sales, reduced manufacturing costs and continued improvement in reducing digital imaging losses.

During the first quarter, U.S. sales increased six percent to $189.3 million from $178.0 million in the same period of 1996. International sales were down to $268.2 million from $283.1 million in the same period last year, primarily due to the strong dollar.

Polaroid also said in its press release that as a result of the change in functional currency and based on a tax rate of 37 percent, it had a $9.9 million, or $.22 per common share, exchange gain from balance sheet translation in the first quarter of 1997.
Polaroid said gains of this magnitude are not expected to recur.
"We are very pleased with the overall first quarter results, especially with the boost in U.S. sales in March," Chairman Gary DiCamillo said.
"We continue to see business gains, albeit tempered by currency, in western Europe, Australia and Japan, in response to stronger marketing efforts there," he said.
U.S. retail camera sales have improved by double-digit gains since November 1996, and the company is gaining confidence in its revamped advertising and promotion program, DiCamillo said.

"Looking out at the next three quarters, we are on track with our plan and are working diligently to achieve the 1997 profit goals we've set," he said. "We are continuing to monitor the effect of the strong U.S. dollar on our business."
